card_reads.read: The board and our number agree in a $16,000 claimer. One horse looks alone on the lead, which our pace adjustment credits. We make the favourite, #7 HARD TO FIGURE, 24% against the board's 31%, shorter than we think it should be. We are not betting the race; take it as an opinion, not a play.
card_reads.shape: One horse looks alone on the lead, clear of the field on the early figures. Uncontested, that is the hardest kind of horse to run down, because nobody makes it work for the lead and it dictates every fraction. Our number credits #8 Pioneer Prince accordingly.

card_reads.read: Ranks #1 in our power figure blend; model 24% vs 12% morning-line implied (+12.4 pts)
card_reads.shape: No one horse is entitled to the lead going a mile and a sixteenth on turf, so expect a tactical early half and a race decided in the lane rather than on the front end. Only one has shown genuine early speed, and without company it may get away with a softer lead than the figures suggest. No pace adjustment applied.

card_reads.read: Ranks #1 in our power figure blend; model 32% vs 27% morning-line implied (+5.5 pts)
card_reads.shape: Nobody is clearly entitled to the lead going five and a half furlongs on dirt, which over a sprint usually means an honest pace rather than a meltdown, and a race run close to the figures. Two have shown early speed without enough of them to rate the race contested, so how hard they go at each other is the open question. No pace adjustment applied.
